name: Convergent cross mapping (CCM)
title: Whose fingerprint is in whose dynamics?
what: If X drives Y, Y's own history remembers X; test whether Y's past can reconstruct X.
pick_line: Reuse neighbour sets so 10,000 surrogates are cheap and the p-value floor drops.
data: Public weekly data (CFTC TFF, NY Fed fails, OFR repo), 2019–2025; descriptive only
one: Fails and leveraged-fund positioning both cross-map the repo spread; Holm-borderline.

left.sub: says positioning and fails drive each other, both ways

right.sub: no cross-map link either way; possibly a shared cycle (untested)

findings.h: The spread's dynamics remember fails and positioning, not the reverse.
findings.t: Cross-map skill at full library: fails → spread 0.33 (reverse 0.16); positioning → spread 0.25 (reverse 0.01). Both converge as the library grows.
findings.note: Both teal links: shift p = 0.005 (the floor with 200 surrogates), Holm p = 0.05.

findings.h: Where Granger sees a two-way link, CCM sees none.
findings.t: Positioning ↔ fails: Granger p = 0.001 and 0.004; CCM p = 0.47 and 0.21. Granger-both-ways with no cross-map skill is the classic sign of a shared linear cycle (untested here).

findings.h: Links into DVP volume appear only after mid-2022.
findings.t: Fails → DVP volume: ρ 0.02 in 2019–22 vs 0.38 in 2022–25, as DVP outstanding roughly doubled. Fails → spread is stable (0.27 / 0.26).
